quandoUsar: A project's history, audit log, or sequence of deploys, where order and recency matter more than comparing fields.
Feeds that receive updates while the screen is open: the new event enters at the top, the others move down, and its title is announced to the screen reader.
When only some events have details worth opening: with `detail`, the row becomes a button that expands in place.
quandoEvitar: Use `sortable-data-table` when people need to sort or compare records by column.
Use `stepper` to show the steps of a flow and what is already complete, not dated events.
Use `notification-center` for notices with read and unread state.

teclado.acao: Move focus to the previous or next row that has `detail`; rows without detail don't receive focus.
Go to the first or last row with detail.
Open or close the focused row's detail.

acessibilidade: The feed is a `region` named by `label`; each day is a `<section>` tied to its heading (`role="heading"` at the `headingLevel` level, 3 by default), and events form an ordered list.
Rows with `detail` are `<button>`s with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the time is a `<time>` with the full date in hidden text, and new events are announced in a `role="status"` region.
`tone` only changes the marker's color: write the outcome in the `title` (“Deploy failed”); the avatar has an empty `alt` because the name already comes in `actor`.
movimento: Each row reveals itself once, on entering the viewport: the marker appears growing and the vertical stroke draws to the next one; rows that appear together enter 90 ms apart.
New events enter at the top, making room while the others move down; the detail opens with a spring on height, the arrow rotates, and the relative time and day count swap by rolling.
With “reduced motion” on, there is no stagger or displacement: markers, strokes, and details appear instantly or with a short fade, and the return to the top is instant.
responsivo: With `maxHeight`, the feed scrolls internally, day headings stick to the top, and the bottom edge fades while there are more events; without it, the feed grows with the page.
If a new event arrives while the feed is scrolled down, it returns to the top on its own; turn this off with `scrollToNew={false}`.
desempenho: There is no virtualization: all events stay in the DOM and each row detects its viewport entry only once; for long histories, limit what is passed in `events`.
notasIA: Pass `events`, `label`, and `now` (epoch ms); the component has no clock of its own, so update `now` from time to time (every minute, for example) so relative times don't go stale.
Days and hours use `timeZone="UTC"` by default: pass the local time zone (`"America/Sao_Paulo"`) and `locale`; “Today”, “Yesterday”, “updates”, and the times `8m` and `Now` stay in English.
Use a stable `id`: it is how an event is recognized as new, animates its entrance, and is announced; on another surface, define `--timeline-surface` for the day headings' background.
